refuted.fact: F46: 「ESMA MiCA 頁面上 Interim MiCA Register 區塊在 2026-09-16 查核時標示『Last update: 9 September 2026』」，verbatim_quote 為 "Last update: 9 September 2026"
refuted.why: On the same stated check date, 2026-09-16, the page carries exactly one 'Last update' string and it reads 'Last update: 16 September 2026'. I fetched https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/markets-crypto-assets-regulation-mica twice (HTTP 200, 88,598 bytes) and grepped for 'Last update' both times; both returned '16 September 2026' and nothing else. The register CSVs behind it carry last-modified Wed, 16 Sep 2026 15:58:32 GMT (CASPS) and 15:58:57 GMT (NCASP), so the 9 September version was live earlier the same day and was replaced during the working day. This is not fabrication — the researcher plainly fetched before 15:58 UTC — but the verbatim_quote is now false against the cited page and would be false in print. A quoted register version date must be re-read at write time and again at publication, or dropped in favour of 'ESMA 說明名冊每週更新' (F45), which is stable.

refuted.fact: F48: 「CASPS.csv（對應 2026-09-09 版名冊）共有 346 筆資料列、342 個不重複的 LEI 代碼……其中 344 筆沒有填寫許可終止日，2 筆有」
refuted.why: The file now served at that URL has 352 data rows and 349 distinct LEIs, of which 350 have no ac_authorisationEndDate and 2 do. I parsed it with Python's csv module over the file handle (not line splitting, which miscounts because ac_serviceCode contains embedded newlines). Two separate defects: (a) the counts are stale by one weekly republication, as above; (b) the recorded pair is internally impossible — with exactly three LEIs each appearing twice, 346 rows must give 343 distinct LEIs, not 342, and there are no blank-LEI rows to absorb the difference (I checked: zero). So even the superseded snapshot had an arithmetic error in it. What does still hold, and can be used: the three duplicated LEIs are EUWAX AG (529900032TYR45XIEW79), Deutsche WertpapierService Bank AG (529900EXG2PM316ISO63) and DekaBank Deutsche Girozentrale (0W2PZJM8XOY22M4GG883); and the only two rows with an authorisation end date are still Stratos Europe Ltd (CY, 24/04/2026, no comment) and Decubate B.V. (NL, 26/03/2026, comment 'Voluntary request to revoke authorisation by the entity').

unsupported.fact: F44（末句）：「為了趕上法定期限，ESMA 先製作 interim MiCA register，以 CSV 檔集合形式發布，直到 2026 年年中正式整合進 ESMA 的資訊系統。」
unsupported.why: The page does say 'until mid-2026 when it will be formally integrated into ESMA's IT systems', so the transcription is accurate — but that is a forward-looking sentence written in 2024 that the same page contradicts on the check date: mid-2026 has passed and the register is still five CSV downloads. Recorded in verified_facts as flat narrative, it reads as an accomplished fact. The researcher did flag exactly this in unverified_or_excluded, which is to their credit, but a writer works from verified_facts first and will not necessarily reach the caveat. Either move the clause out of verified_facts, or restate it as what it is: 'ESMA 的說明頁至今仍寫著名冊會在 2026 年年中整合進其資訊系統，但查核日（2026-09-16）該頁提供的仍是五個 CSV 檔下載。' The first half of F44 (Articles 109 and 110, central register of white papers, authorised CASPs and non-compliant entities, by 30 December 2024, data supplied by NCAs and EBA) is fully confirmed.

unsupported.fact: F50 的可重現性（數字本身經我重算仍成立）
unsupported.why: Not an error: I re-derived every figure against the live file and they all still hold — earliest ac_authorisationNotificationDate 30/12/2024; June 2026 = 75, the largest single month (next is December 2025 at 44); July 2026 = 31; August 2026 = 17. But the fact is pinned to a register version that the URL no longer serves, so it is unreproducible by anyone checking the record later, and that it survived the republication is luck, not design. One substantive addition: the record's unverified_or_excluded excludes ONE impossible future-dated row (Volksbank Baumberge eG, 06/10/2026). The live file now has TWO — the other is Deutsche Bank Aktiengesellschaft, 12/10/2026 — and September 2026 now carries 8 rows. If the article keeps any month-by-month figure, re-derive it at write time and exclude both future-dated rows, not one.

additional_findings: MISSED FIRST-PARTY SOURCE, and it is the one that most changes what this article can safely say: ESMA Q&A 2220, https://www.esma.europa.eu/publications-data/questions-answers/2220 (HTTP 200, answer dated 04-07-2024, Additional Legal Reference 143(3)), 'Entities not authorised as CASPs by the end of the transition period'. It answers the obvious reader question that MiCA Article 143(3)'s own wording invites: what if the firm applied in time but the NCA has not decided? ESMA: 'Where an entity providing crypto-asset services in accordance with applicable law before 30 December 2024 has not been authorised as a CASP by the end of the transition period applicable in the relevant Member State, they must cease providing crypto-asset services until they are granted authorisation as a CASP under MiCA.' A pending application does NOT extend the period. Without this Q&A a writer reading only F2 ('until 1 July 2026 or until they are granted or refused an authorisation pursuant to Article 63, whichever is sooner') can easily reach the opposite conclusion and print it. This Q&A is linked directly from the Interactive Single Rulebook Article 143 page the record says it fetched.

MISSED FIRST-PARTY SOURCE, pairs with the above: ESMA Q&A 2221, https://www.esma.europa.eu/publications-data/questions-answers/2221 (HTTP 200, 04-07-2024), 'Entities who have not applied for, or whose application for authorisation as CASPs has been refused by the end of the transition period'. 'Where such entities do not seek a MiCA authorisation, they should consider at an early stage how they will wind down their operations in a manner that avoids negative impact on their clients in accordance, if relevant, with applicable laws.' This is ESMA saying the wind-down expectation in the 2025-12, 2026-04 and 2026-06 statements was already on the record in July 2024 — useful for section 4 and cheap to source.

MISSED FIRST-PARTY SOURCE that directly qualifies F54: ESMA Q&A 2070, https://www.esma.europa.eu/publications-data/questions-answers/2070 (HTTP 200, 20-06-2024, Additional Legal Reference 143(6), answer provided by the European Commission), 'Simplified authorisation procedures'. Two things F54 does not say. First, what 'simplified' means: 'information that was submitted by the entity in order to obtain authorisation under national law does not need to be submitted again as part of the authorisation process set out in Article 63 MiCA', so the procedure differs from one Member State to another depending on what that State asked for before 30 December 2024. Second, and this is the sharp limit: 'Article 143(6) does not provide for the possibility to put in place a simplified procedure for applications where the crypto-asset service providers were not authorised but merely registered at national level. Under the AML/CFT framework, Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs) are registered, rather than authorised as prescribed under Article 143(6) MiCA. Therefore, registration under the AML/CFT framework should not be considered sufficient to benefit from the aforementioned simplified procedure.' The record's corrections_to_candidate_list rightly proposes adding 143(6) to the article; if it is added, it must be added with this limit, or the article will imply every grandfathered VASP had a fast lane.

MISSED FIRST-PARTY SOURCE: ESMA Q&A 2068, https://www.esma.europa.eu/publications-data/questions-answers/2068 (HTTP 200, 20-06-2024, Article 143(3), European Commission answer), 'Grandfathering clause and applicable AML laws'. Confirms that entities registered under national AML/CFT transposition arrangements DO fall within 'in accordance with applicable law' for Article 143(3) purposes, and states the territorial limit in one clean sentence: 'The entities authorised under national law before 30 December 2024 do not benefit from a passporting regime under MiCA but can provide crypto-asset services within the jurisdiction they are registered in.' That is a more quotable statement of the article's central 'no passport' point than the Q&A 2086 wording the record uses, and it is a Commission answer rather than an ESMA one.

MISSED FIRST-PARTY SOURCE: ESMA Q&A 2085, https://www.esma.europa.eu/publications-data/questions-answers/2085 (HTTP 200, 29-01-2024, Article 143), 'New CASPs established before (and after) 30 December 2024'. 'There is no effective date of initiation related to entry into force or other temporal constraint (i.e., if the entity providing crypto services began offering services in 2014, it would still be eligible for grandfathering).' Closes the 'how old did the firm have to be' question that 30 December 2024 invites.

MATERIAL CONTENT MISSING FROM THE RECORD, on a source that IS in sources[]: the 2026-04-17 statement's expectations for ALREADY-AUTHORISED CASPs are absent from all 56 verified_facts. The record captures only the unauthorised side. ESMA: 'ESMA also expects authorised CASPs to actively manage the migration of existing clients ahead of 1 July 2026. In particular, authorised CASPs should take the necessary steps to onboard existing EU clients before the end of the transitional period. In doing so, ESMA expects authorised CASPs to apply robust onboarding processes to ensure full compliance with applicable AML/CFT requirements.' Half of the deadline's mechanics — where the clients were supposed to go — is missing.

MATERIAL CONTENT MISSING, same document: the quality bar ESMA sets for a wind-down plan, which F37 reduces to a date. 'Wind-down plans enable an orderly exit without causing undue economic harm to clients, including by arranging the offboarding of clients – for example by organising the transfer of crypto-assets held on their behalf to an authorised CASP or to a self-hosted wallet. CASPs should provide existing clients with prior notice before implementing the wind-down plan. Plans should be operational, credible, and immediately executable and designed in accordance with all relevant EU conduct, prudential and AML/CFT obligations.' The prior-notice requirement in particular is the one thing in these documents an affected customer can check against their own inbox.

MATERIAL CONTENT MISSING, same document: the consumer warning's framing sentence and its closing line, both absent from F43. Opening: 'ESMA wishes to warn investors engaging with crypto assets that not all providers are authorised under MiCA after 1 July 2026, and that your protections depend on who you are dealing with.' Closing: 'Staying with an unauthorised provider may mean less legal protection and a greater risk of losing access to your assets.' Also footnote 5 of that statement, which the record does not carry: 'This applies irrespective whether the MiCA has been implemented in a Member State or not' — a second, differently-worded instance of the point F35 records from the June statement.

GRANDFATHERING TABLE, independently re-derived: every figure in F14–F19 is correct. 27 EU Member States and 3 EEA countries; 18 months for 15 States (Belgium, Bulgaria, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Greece, Spain, France, Croatia, Italy, Cyprus, Luxembourg, Malta, Portugal, Romania), 12 months for 5 (Germany, Ireland, Lithuania, Austria, Slovakia), 9 months for Sweden alone, 6 months for 6 (Latvia, Hungary, Netherlands, Poland, Slovenia, Finland); Iceland 18, Liechtenstein 18, Norway 12. 15+5+1+6 = 27. All five footnotes verbatim-correct, and the country-to-asterisk mapping is right (** Bulgaria, *** Czechia, **** Denmark, ***** Italy). The record's not_said entry about the orphan single-asterisk footnote is a genuine and good catch: the '*' carrying 'To be able to benefit from the grandfathering period, applicant CASPs must apply before 8 October 2025' is unattributable, because the only other '*' in the document is on the title, pointing at the general caveat, and no country row carries one. Worth recording as an observation but still not assignable: that orphan date, 8 October 2025, is the same date as Bulgaria's '**' application deadline. Do not infer from that.

The 'EU-wide vs national' date discipline is sound, which is the thing this article most needed to get right. event_date 2026-07-01 traces to statutory text ('until 1 July 2026', Article 143(3), first subparagraph, Interactive Single Rulebook) and to ESMA's own framing in both 2026 statements; the 2026-06-23 publication date of the wind-down statement and the 2026-04-17 date of the earlier one are kept distinct from it in event_date_basis and never used as the event date; the national variation is carried as month counts only, with the calendar-date arithmetic explicitly refused in unverified_or_excluded and must_not_write; and the EEA three are kept out of 'across the EU'. I found no date conflation anywhere in the record.

TRANSLATION PRECISION, MiCA Article 3(1)(16) in F53: 'exchange of crypto-assets for funds' is rendered 「以資金兌換加密資產」 and 'exchange of crypto-assets for other crypto-assets' 「以其他加密資產兌換加密資產」, both of which reverse the direction of the statutory phrase. The article enumerates a service by its statutory name, so write 「加密資產與資金的兌換」 and 「加密資產與其他加密資產的兌換」. The other eight limbs (a, b, e, f, g, h, i, j) are rendered correctly, and the list is complete and in the right order.

VERBATIM CHECK, all 33 verbatim_quote values: I compared every one character by character against my own fetch, normalising only PDF extraction artefacts (injected spaces inside hyphenated words such as 'crypto -asset', curly-to-straight quotes, en dash). 31 are exact. F46 is refuted above. The remaining one, F33, silently drops an in-span footnote marker: the source reads 'or solicit EU clients3. This also applies', the quote reads 'or solicit EU clients. This also applies'. Nothing hinges on it and the elision is of a superscript reference only — flagged for completeness, not as a defect requiring a fix. Notably, the traps the other checkers hit did not occur here: F9 preserves ESMA's own hyphenated 'grand-fathering' rather than silently normalising it to 'grandfathering', and no quote joins non-contiguous or reordered spans.

The record enumerates the interim register's five CSV files correctly (F45), but only four were downloaded. The MiCA page also links a sixth file at that path, Description_of_the_fields_in_the_interim_MiCA_register.csv, and the Title II white-paper download is OTHER.csv, which was not fetched. Nothing in the article depends on it; noted so a later checker does not read the four-file fetch as the whole register.

REPO NOTE, not a fact defect: crypto.md states the crypto workspace is docs/crypto-news-2026/, but this record and all 35 sibling fact-checks live under docs/news-2026-batch-4/. The writer should follow the batch-4 path that is actually in use and not create docs/crypto-news-2026/ on the strength of the spec line.

There is still no crypto index article, so the record's warning stands: the first link must point at an index slug that actually exists by the time this pack is written, not an invented one.
corrections_to_candidate_list: C2 一手來源第二條寫「（2026-04）」，應寫 2026-04-17：PDF 標頭「17 April 2026 / ESMA75-113276571-1679」與 2026-06-23 聲明註腳 1 都是這個日期。研究紀錄已提出此更正，我實抓確認無誤。

C2 要點「祖父條款只在原會員國有效、沒有 passporting」在列出的三條一手來源裡一條都找不到——我對三份 PDF 全文搜尋 'passport'，零命中。真正的一手依據是 ESMA Q&A 2086（2024-01-29）、Q&A 2068（2024-06-20，執委會答覆，措辭最乾淨）與 2023-10-17 聲明的註腳 10。研究紀錄指出了這點，但它寫「列出的兩條一手來源」，候選清單其實列了三條。
C2 沒有列 Q&A 2220 與 2221（皆 2024-07-04）。2220 是本題最關鍵的一條：已提出申請但主管機關尚未決定者，過渡期屆滿仍必須停止提供服務，不得以「申請中」繼續營業。建議補進要點，否則單看第 143(3) 條文很容易寫反。
C2 沒有提第 143(6) 條簡化許可程序；若補進來，必須一併補 Q&A 2070 的限制：僅限 2024-12-30 當日已依國內法「取得許可」者，AML/CFT 架構下的 VASP「登記」不符合資格。

各國過渡期對照表的網址路徑是 /2024-12/，但它是活文件：內部 ModDate 2026-05-19、伺服器 last-modified 2026-05-20。研究紀錄已記錄。更需要標註的是 Interim MiCA Register：CASPS.csv 與 NCASP.csv 的 last-modified 是 2026-09-16 15:58 UTC，也就是查核當天被換掉，網址固定、舊版不可回溯。候選清單若要用名冊家數，必須註明「依查核當天 ESMA 顯示的名冊版本」並在定稿當天重算。
候選清單「讀者角度」寫「台灣讀者用到的歐洲平台可能因此停止對歐盟客戶服務」——取得的 ESMA 文件全部只談 EU clients，沒有一句談非歐盟居民使用歐盟業者的影響，也沒有點名任何業者。研究紀錄的 not_said 已正確擋下這點；候選清單本身的措辭應一併修掉，否則下一個撰稿者會照著寫。
